screens.name: Home — default, no omen, populated omen, enlarged and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 21–22 show the gold orb dominating Home, with readable instructions and distinct populated and empty omen states; supplied runtime reports browser size and contrast checks.
findings: Give the enlarged omen more immediate visibility by reducing decorative vertical space while preserving text scaling.

screens.name: Approach — normal, enlarged and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 shows the opening status beneath the orb, with centered normal text becoming a substantially larger left-aligned block.
findings: Preserve a more consistent text alignment across sizes to strengthen continuity into the question flow.

screens.name: Question composer — self, named person, collapsed and compose-read variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 01–03, 13 and 41 show question-first layouts with a prominent submit action, while supplied runtime reports retained drafts and reachable enlarged controls.
findings: Reduce discretionary vertical spacing so the alternative voice action is easier to discover at 200%.

screens.name: Named-person editor — selected Someone, populated name, normal and enlarged
screens.evidence: Sheets 02–03 and 22 show explicit selection, a labeled Alex input and privacy guidance; supplied runtime reports invalid-name rejection, cancellation and focus return.
findings: Keep Cancel changes closer to the primary action in the enlarged layout so reversal is easier to discover.

screens.name: Voice entry — microphone failure and retry
screens.evidence: Sheet 23 shows an explicit voice-start failure, a dominant typing fallback and a separate retry action at both text sizes.
findings: Replace the generic introductory heading with a concise failure heading when voice cannot start.

screens.name: Adaptive card 1 — plan readiness
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows progress, one question and four choices, with the orb removed from the enlarged view and selection feedback described in supplied runtime.
findings: Trim excess heading-to-option spacing at 200% so the last choice has more breathing room above the viewport edge.

screens.name: Adaptive card 2 — obstacle
screens.evidence: Sheets 08–09 show a clear second-step indicator and consistently separated obstacle choices across settled and transition captures.
findings: Retain a visible selected acknowledgment long enough for users to connect their choice with the next card.

screens.name: Adaptive card 3 — support
screens.evidence: Sheets 09–10 show the third-step indicator and explicit wording that choosing an answer reveals the forecast.
findings: Validate that the brief selection acknowledgment remains perceptible before the final loading transition.

screens.name: Adaptive card — custom answer, empty and disabled
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 shows a labeled answer field, disabled Continue with explanatory guidance and Back to choices; supplied runtime reports long-draft retention and constrained-height reachability.
findings: Separate Back to choices more clearly from the progress count in the enlarged header.

screens.name: Planning — loading and cancellation
screens.evidence: Sheets 29–30 show a named processing stage, a one-minute expectation, credit reassurance and cancellation, with timeout and cancellation behavior reported in runtime.
findings: Shorten the enlarged explanatory copy to reduce the distance between the status and Cancel.

screens.name: Research — loading and cancellation
screens.evidence: Sheets 30–31 distinguish research from planning through stage-specific text while preserving the same loading composition.
findings: Make the change from checking the question to forming the forecast more visually explicit.

screens.name: Planning error — retry and edit
screens.evidence: Sheet 15 shows a compact error screen with a dominant retry, a question-edit route and explicit assurance that nothing was charged.
findings: Preserve this recovery hierarchy when real provider messages replace the labeled fixture.

screens.name: Prediction error — retry, review answers and edit
screens.evidence: Sheets 15–16 add Review answers to the retry and editing routes without introducing competing filled buttons.
findings: Keep retry tied to the retained question and answers so recovery does not require re-entry.

screens.name: Sensitive request — planning and prediction variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 33–34 foreground support, retain alternative-question and editing routes, and disclose that no reading or memory was spent.
findings: Move the credit and memory reassurance higher in the enlarged layout so it is easier to encounter.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — normal, enlarged and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 32–33 show the forecast, speculative label, reminder date and prominent Share action, with several subsequent actions carrying similar visual weight.
findings: Group editing and review actions behind one clearly labeled secondary section to reduce competition after the reveal.

screens.name: Check-in — unanswered
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 places the outcome question before explanation and sharing, although the enlarged forecast pushes later outcome choices below the captured viewport.
findings: Label the date as a reminder rather than an apparent forecast deadline to distinguish it from the spring prediction.

screens.name: Check-in — Yes saved
screens.evidence: Sheet 28 shows both a saved confirmation and a check beside Yes, with persistence represented separately in History.
findings: Use the same outcome wording in the selected row, saved confirmation and history entry.

screens.name: Check-in — Not quite saved
screens.evidence: Sheet 28 shows Saved · Not quite and a corresponding selected row without replacing the other choices.
findings: Make it explicit that selecting another outcome updates the saved answer.

screens.name: Check-in — Not yet saved, normal and enlarged
screens.evidence: Sheets 28 and 40–41 show a saved pending outcome and precise guidance that the reading remains open and its reminder date is unchanged.
findings: Retain the pending explanation immediately after the choices at every supported text size.

screens.name: Evidence overview — collapsed forecast context
screens.evidence: Sheets 13, 31 and 41–42 show four clearly separated evidence destinations with counts and a collapsed Which forecast disclosure.
findings: Keep a short forecast identifier visible without requiring users to expand Which forecast.

screens.name: Evidence overview — expanded forecast context
screens.evidence: Sheet 42 shows the expanded forecast and speculative label below the evidence list, including an enlarged scrolled capture.
findings: Place the contextual forecast above the evidence categories so users establish context before choosing a reader.

screens.name: Evidence reader — Why this forecast, free and Plus
screens.evidence: Sheets 14, 18 and 32–33 show separated reasoning paragraphs, navigation and speculative labeling, with long synthetic text explicitly identified as layout evidence.
findings: Add concise paragraph labels distinguishing supplied context, inference and limitations.

screens.name: Evidence reader — answers, named prompts and legacy Answer N
screens.evidence: Sheets 12 and 16–17 show both prompt-labeled answers and neutral legacy numbering, while supplied runtime reports retained full content and no guessed legacy semantics.
findings: Explain once why legacy answers use numbers so the missing question labels do not appear accidental.

screens.name: Evidence reader — assumptions
screens.evidence: Sheets 12 and 17 show a simple assumptions reader with speculative labeling and a return route at normal size.
findings: Present each real assumption as a discrete item to make long enlarged content easier to scan.

screens.name: Evidence reader — current sources
screens.evidence: Sheets 14 and 18–19 separate publisher, date, body and source link and explicitly state that background sources do not verify the forecast.
findings: Give each Open source link a source-specific accessible name and preserve that distinction through repeated entries.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 20–21 show an explicit empty state, local-storage explanation and direct Ask the Ball route at both sizes.
findings: Give Ask the Ball a stronger button treatment to make the empty-state next step unmistakable.

screens.name: History — populated, stress list and persisted outcome
screens.evidence: Sheets 19–20 show dated rows, original questions, forecasts, reminder dates and a persisted Came true outcome.
findings: Reduce the enlarged forecast's relative emphasis so each row's status and Open check-in action are easier to locate.

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheets 23–24 show an explicit age question and two unambiguous choices, accompanied by the phrase Teen-safe defaults apply.
findings: Explain the practical effect of teen-safe defaults in plain language or omit that unexplained term here.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–25 show labeled birthday parts and a skip route, with enlarged fields stacking vertically and moving the actions below the initial viewport.
findings: Explain what Continue does with an empty optional birthday, since Skip for now offers an apparently equivalent route.

screens.name: Onboarding — age blocked
screens.evidence: Sheet 25 clearly states the age restriction and provides a correction route without displaying an ordinary continuation action.
findings: Ensure the correction label matches whether the user supplied a birthday or only selected an age category.

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday correction
screens.evidence: Sheet 26 shows actual-birthday guidance, separate date fields, Check birthday and a return route, with validation behavior reported in supplied runtime.
findings: Reduce discretionary spacing in the enlarged form to shorten the distance from the year field to validation.

screens.name: Onboarding — focus unselected and selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 26–28 show explicit optionality, a checked selected focus and a primary label that changes from Continue without a focus to Meet the Ball.
findings: Keep the optionality guidance and progress indicator easy to recover when enlarged layouts scroll.

screens.name: You — profile, plan and remembered focus
screens.evidence: Sheets 44–45 distinguish birth profile, plan balance and remembered focus with edit and forget actions.
findings: Strengthen section separation so profile data, billing and remembered information scan as three distinct groups.

screens.name: You — birthday editing
screens.evidence: Sheet 44 shows populated birthday fields, Save birthday, Cancel changes and a subordinate Remove birthday disclosure.
findings: Clarify the consequences of removing the birthday in the disclosure before the destructive action.

screens.name: Birth details — initial and editing form
screens.evidence: Sheets 04–06 and 43 show the optional form, saved-chart retention guidance and city-selection prerequisite, while runtime reports exact text scaling and form focus checks.
findings: Use an unmistakable empty-time placeholder so 14:30 cannot be mistaken for an already supplied birth time.

screens.name: Birth details — city results
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 shows multiple Copenhagen results distinguished by region and country, with live lookup and selected-city collapse reported in runtime.
findings: Add a short Choose your birth city instruction above the result list.

screens.name: Birth details — invalid time with selected city
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 shows 25:99 with the precise accepted range and retained city; supplied runtime reports field focus, aria-invalid, contrast checks and normal/enlarged testing.
findings: Keep the error adjacent to the time field and preserve the selected city through correction.

screens.name: Birth details — search unavailable and retry
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows an explicit unavailable message, Retry city search and an unavailable save action, with controlled failure and actual-service recovery reported.
findings: Keep the failure explanation close to Retry city search in enlarged scrolled views.

screens.name: Birth details — no city results
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 distinguishes no matching city from service failure and suggests trying a nearby town.
findings: Place the no-results guidance directly beside the city input so it remains contextual at 200%.

screens.name: Birth details — calculated and saved, including successful retry
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows a dedicated saved result with signs, place/time and Done, while runtime reports actual calculation, reload persistence and focus transfer to the heading.
findings: Capitalize the sign names consistently with Gemini Sun elsewhere in the profile.

screens.name: Birth details — forgotten
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 confirms time and place were forgotten while still displaying 14:30 in the time field; runtime states the saved values were cleared and birthday retained.
findings: Replace the concrete-looking 14:30 placeholder after deletion with HH:MM to remove the apparent contradiction.

screens.name: Settings — controls and empty memory
screens.evidence: Sheet 35 shows labeled sound, motion and large-text switches alongside plan, privacy and deletion routes, with the enlarged switch visibly selected.
findings: Separate destructive data deletion from ordinary preferences with an explicit section label.

screens.name: Sky — offline samples, selected star and question
screens.evidence: Sheet 39 labels the sky as offline sample content, shows a selected Love star and question, and replaces the constellation with a vertical arrangement at 200%.
findings: Reduce enlarged star-row spacing so users can reach the selected question with less scrolling.

screens.name: Circles — offline and empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 shows offline status, Retry, disabled creation and unavailable eligibility with a clear summary of shared information.
findings: Explain eligibility in user language beside the disabled Friends can ask about me control.

screens.name: Plans — selected yearly, monthly and reading packs
screens.evidence: Sheet 29 clearly marks simulation, yearly selection, recurring prices and separate reading packs, while actual payment behavior remains outside the evidence.
findings: Repeat the no-real-payment cue next to the enlarged primary action because the introductory explanation is outside that capture.

screens.name: Share — default preview and expanded invite/reminder options
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–39 and 42–43 show preview enlargement, Download image, explicit privacy boundaries and separate invitation and reminder tools.
findings: Reduce preview-to-action spacing so enlarged users encounter Download image sooner.

screens.name: Share export — preparing
screens.evidence: Sheets 35–36 show disabled download with Preparing image, and runtime reports one actual held encode, duplicate prevention and continued availability of other tools.
findings: Keep the preparing status adjacent to the button throughout scrolling and text enlargement.

screens.name: Share export — failed and retry
screens.evidence: Sheet 36 shows explicit export failure and Try download again, with a deliberate encoder failure followed by a real successful PNG retry reported.
findings: Retain the preview and privacy explanation while retrying, as demonstrated.

screens.name: Share export — download started
screens.evidence: Sheets 35–36 accurately report Image download started rather than claiming delivery, with real browser PNG download reported in runtime.
findings: Preserve the distinction between starting a browser download and completing an OS share.

screens.name: Shared image inspection — story and inspection variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 37 and 40 show an enlarged exported image with speculative labeling and a separate Image text section beginning below it.
findings: Offer an immediate jump to Image text so enlarged users need not scroll through the full fixed-size artwork first.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: Home and loading sheets consistently use an illustrated orb, with supplied runtime reporting smooth browser motion and reduced-motion handling.
findings: Keep an explicit text action associated with the interactive Home orb so its function does not depend on illustration recognition.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Main-screen sheets show icon-and-text navigation with gold and underline selection, and runtime reports measured targets of at least 44×44.
findings: Verify the enlarged bar's raised Ask orb never covers the final focused content row during scrolling.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Headers consistently show branding or page title opposite balance, with enlarged reading balances wrapping to two lines.
findings: Reduce the balance block's visual prominence at 200% without reducing its text scale.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: Cream filled buttons consistently identify primary actions, while disabled, preparing and retry variants and browser target checks are supplied.
findings: Preserve the single filled-action hierarchy and explanatory text for disabled states.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold links and white separator rows both represent secondary actions across reveal, settings, forms and sharing.
findings: Standardize which secondary actions use gold links versus full-width white rows.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Card sheets show generous separated choices, with supplied runtime describing a 180ms selected acknowledgment and duplicate prevention.
findings: Confirm the brief acknowledgment is perceptible without relying on animation or color alone.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Composer captures show a persistent label and visible outline, with runtime reporting draft retention, exact scaling and corrected focus-outline spacing.
findings: Apply the same clear input affordance when the populated field is unfocused.

components.name: Large-text input
components.evidence: Enlarged name, question and custom-answer fields retain visible text and borders, with constrained-height draft and submission checks reported.
findings: Reduce surrounding layout spacing before reducing any enlarged input content or text.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheet 35 shows labeled switches with both thumb-position and color changes, while runtime reports control-target measurements.
findings: Confirm the full labeled row activates its switch and exposes the current state to browser assistive technology.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheets 21–22 distinguish an actual omen from No omen today and provide an alternative action in the empty state.
findings: Keep the empty-state explanation visible sooner in the enlarged Home layout.

components.name: Sky stars and selected question
components.evidence: Sheet 39 uses a check and gold styling for Love and repeats its category above the selected sample question.
findings: Make the enlarged category list more compact while maintaining measured touch targets.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheet 11 separates offline recovery, circle creation and friend-question eligibility, with explicit disabled controls.
findings: Replace Eligibility unavailable offline with a concrete explanation of what cannot currently be checked.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheets 19–20 show a stable row structure for question, forecast, reminder or outcome, and check-in navigation.
findings: Keep the row's outcome and navigation visually close to its forecast at 200%.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheet 29 uses a check and gold rule for the yearly option and states both the annual charge and monthly equivalent.
findings: Keep billing cadence and total charge adjacent when the option stacks at enlarged text.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: Share sheets show a bordered story image, enlargement affordance and persistent speculative warning inside the exported artwork.
findings: Provide direct access to scalable image text alongside the fixed-ratio preview.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Error, offline, invalid-time and export sheets identify distinct failures and offer contextual retry, correction or alternative routes.
findings: Keep every explanation beside the control that resolves it when enlarged content scrolls.

components.name: Typography and spacing system
components.evidence: The deck consistently pairs display serif headings with sans-serif body text, and runtime reports exact doubling and sampled contrast passes.
findings: Tune enlarged spacing separately from text scale to reduce oversized heading blocks and long travel to secondary controls.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: All sheets preserve borderless dark mist and a restrained gold glow, with runtime reporting contrast sampling and reduced-motion and isolated performance passes.
findings: Preserve the quiet backing behind body text as atmospheric artwork changes.

components.name: Birthday input
components.evidence: Birthday screens label day, month and year independently and stack them at 200%, with runtime reporting exact scaling and validation coverage.
findings: Reduce excess vertical spacing between stacked date parts so form actions are easier to reach.

components.name: Age confirmation
components.evidence: Sheets 23–25 show explicit age-category choices and a separate blocked state with a correction route.
findings: Maintain equivalent clarity and target size for the under-age choice despite its secondary styling.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Sheets 26–28 show unselected and checked choices with explicit skipping and a changed continuation label, supported by supplied browser selection evidence.
findings: Preserve the checkmark and explicit no-focus path as the selection list evolves.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: Sheets 07 and 44–45 show calculated signs, birth information and explicit edit or forget actions, with local persistence reported.
findings: Standardize sign capitalization and consistently distinguish calculated signs from supplied birth details.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: Sheets 04–07 and 43 cover initial, results, invalid, failed, saved and forgotten states, with browser focus, error semantics and persistence checks reported.
findings: Replace the example-like time value with a format placeholder and keep examples exclusively in helper text.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Sheets 02–03 and 22 combine selection, named input and privacy guidance, with invalid-name rejection and draft/focus preservation reported.
findings: Keep selection, name validation and cancellation feedback associated with the same editor.

components.name: Evidence disclosure
components.evidence: Sheets 31–33 and 42 show collapsed and expanded disclosure indicators, evidence destinations and return navigation.
findings: Use a destination chevron for navigation and reserve up/down indicators for inline expansion.

components.name: Export status
components.evidence: Sheets 35–36 show preparing, failed and download-started messages, backed by reported actual encoder blocking, duplicate prevention and successful retry.
findings: Retain the precise download-started wording and one status message per export attempt.

components.name: Close and back controls
components.evidence: The deck alternates icon-only close/back controls with named return actions, and supplied runtime reports target sizing and selected focus-return journeys.
findings: Verify distinct accessible names and predictable destinations for Close, Back and Back to forecast.

components.name: Progress indicator
components.evidence: Sheets 08–10 pair segmented gold progress with explicit 1 of 3 through 3 of 3 labels.
findings: Expose the current step as text to assistive technology without redundantly announcing decorative segments.

limitations: All scores are provisional browser assessments; supplied runtime claims were considered but not independently replayed.
Screen entries group corresponding normal, enlarged, transition and explicitly named variants; component scores assess their shared implementation across the supplied deck.

The schema has no aggregate fields; A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces, F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility, and overall is 0.4A + 0.6F with null dimensions excluded.
The requested A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across all screens and components; this conclusion is not caused solely by deferred native testing.
Static transition frames support visual comparison but cannot establish temporal continuity; supplied browser motion evidence supports only the reported tested behavior.
Scrolled or viewport-cropped captures do not establish unreachable controls; supplied reachability checks were considered, and no hard-gate failure is established by the deck.
The forgotten time's visible 14:30 is a clarity concern, not evidence that deletion failed; runtime explicitly reports successful removal.
Synthetic repeated, truncated and fixture-labeled content was treated as geometry evidence, not as a production-copy or predictive-quality finding.
Physical iPhone, VoiceOver, native text scaling, software keyboard behavior, microphone success, haptics, OS sharing and actual payments remain unverified.
Sky and Circles demonstrate honest offline/sample states; these captures do not establish production social, cloud or authentication behavior.
No novice-user study, independent predictive-accuracy evidence or full native 9/10 certification is present.
The permitted supporting files were not inspected; this evaluation uses the supplied screenshots and runtime statement only.
topFixes: Remove the apparent deletion contradiction by replacing the birth-time placeholder 14:30 with HH:MM.
Tune spacing at 200% while preserving exact text enlargement, especially around birthday fields, composer alternatives, share previews and large headings.
Simplify the reveal's secondary actions and standardize navigation versus inline-disclosure indicators.
Keep forecast identity visible in evidence views and distinguish reminder dates from prediction deadlines.
Keep errors and recovery explanations adjacent to their relevant controls in enlarged scrolled layouts.
Complete browser assistive-technology and representative user checks before claiming effortless interaction, then perform the separately deferred native verification.
